subject: Dedicated cluster footprint intake — LunarPay pilot
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara@lunarpay.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Chen <mchen@lunarpay.com>, LunarPay Procurement <procurement@lunarpay.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot sizing request — LunarPay tokenization & fraud model

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. LunarPay is excited to move forward with a small dedicated pilot to validate inference cost and tail latency for our transaction-scoring model. Before we book a technical workshop, can you confirm what inputs you need to build a conservative capacity model?

Quick summary of our current expectations:
- Peak online score QPS: ~420 QPS sustained for 30s bursts (spikes to ~1200 QPS for ~5s)
- Concurrent active users (sessions): ~5k, but only ~8% hit the scoring path at once
- Typical prompt length: 55 tokens (pre-context) + 750 token feature serialization
- Average generated response: 60 tokens (mostly short structured JSON)
- Hard latency SLO: 150ms p95 for single-request path, 50ms p50 is a nice-to-have
- Persistence: KV cache beneficial for repeated tokens across sessions (we have shared user prefixes)

I've attached a 24-hour sampled trace and a short sample_prompts.txt that shows our typical request shape. Please let me know if this is enough to produce a first-cut GPU footprint and an agenda for the workshop.

Thanks —
Sara Liu
Technical Program Manager, LunarPay
attachments: lunarpay_token_trace.json (24h sample), sample_prompts.txt
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara@lunarpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing request — LunarPay tokenization & fraud model

Hi Sara —

Appreciate the detailed notes and the trace. That should be enough to get a conservative first-pass footprint. Attached is a short intake we use to normalize traces into the sizing matrix (redwood-dedicated-intake.pdf). Could you confirm three items so we can lock assumptions?
1) What % of requests include the full 750-token feature serialization vs. a short summary (~120 tokens)?
2) Do you expect any of the scoring calls to use function/tool-calls or streaming responses (we treat streaming differently for batching)?
3) Any regulatory constraints that require on-prem or strictly VPC-isolated Private deployment during pilot?

Next steps: Marissa (cc'd) will run the trace through our capacity estimator and propose a recommended GPU SKU mix and an estimated node count for the pilot. If the numbers look reasonable we'll book a 90-min workshop to walk through caching strategy and rollout plan.

Available times for a workshop next week: Tue 6/6 10:00-11:30 PT or Wed 6/7 09:00-10:30 PT — does either work?

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-dedicated-intake.pdf
From: Sara Liu <sara@lunarpay.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Chen <mchen@lunarpay.com>, LunarPay Procurement <procurement@lunarpay.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing request — LunarPay tokenization & fraud model

Diego and team —

Answers inline:
1) ~70% of calls include the full 750-token serialization, 30% are ~120 tokens.
2) No streaming; synchronous JSON response only. No external tooling invoked.
3) Pilot must be VPC-only (Private deployment) but we can coordinate a temporary VPC peering for the workshop.

Workshop: Tue 6/6 10:00 PT works for us. Mark from procurement is on copy to coordinate order forms and initial compliance paperwork.

Thanks,
Sara
attachments: lunarpay_token_trace.json, sample_prompts.txt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara@lunarpay.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: LunarPay — first-pass GPU footprint & questions

Hi Sara —

I ran your 24h trace through our estimator with the 70/30 split and synchronous-only constraint. High-level first-pass estimate for a 2-week pilot (non-prod, VPC-isolated):
- Recommended primary GPU: 2 x A100-80GB (per pool node) for best NVMe caching and long-sequence performance
- Suggested cluster: 3 active nodes + 1 hot-standby (total 4) to hit 420 QPS sustained with room for 5s spikes to 1200 QPS using our continuous-batching path
- Expected token throughput: ~5.6M tokens/min peak across cluster during spikes
- Estimated p95 latency (single-request path): 110–160ms depending on cache hit rate; with 60% prefix reuse we'd expect ~105–125ms p95
- Monthly pilot estimated cost (pro-rata): spreadsheet attached (lunarpay_dedicated_estimate.xlsx)

Questions to refine sizing:
- Can you confirm the observed 5s spikes are correlated to batch settlement windows (e.g., morning batch job) vs genuine synchronous user bursts? If it's batch-driven we can recommend a separate batch-queue to drain these without affecting p95 for interactive users.
- Do you control request fanout? If the scoring call fans out several sub-requests we need to account for multiplication factor.

I'll present this in the workshop and walk through tradeoffs: batch versus stricter CPU/GPU concurrency, cache TTLs, and fallback policies. Dev, can you prepare the expected profiler output and a caching strategy sketch for the session?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
attachments: lunarpay_dedicated_estimate.xlsx
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LunarPay — first-pass GPU footprint & questions

Marissa —

I'll pull the profiler output and a 3-slide caching sketch (KV prefix strategy + suggested TTLs) and attach to the workshop invite. Initial note: if LunarPay can canonicalize the 750-token serialization (stable ordering and normalized fields) we should see prefix reuse closer to 70% across sessions which materially lowers cost. Also: recommend enabling our token-level diagnostic traces for 48h in the pilot to validate the 5s spike pattern.

Dev Patel
Staff Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference (Solutions)
From: Sara Liu <sara@lunarpay.com>
